title: Maintaining Proper DWV Pipe Slope
description: Maintaining correct horizontal pipe slope is critical for consistent waste transport in gravity drainage systems. If a drain pipe lacks adequate pitch, wastewater moves too slowly, allowing heavy suspended solids to settle and build up over time. Conversely, an excessively steep pipe pitch allows liquid waste to flow ahead of solid matter, stranding solids in the pipe interior. Professional installers strictly follow local building codes and verify pipe grade using torpedo levels or laser levels during hanger installation, ensuring water and solids move together smoothly without causing siphoning or structural blockages.

Maintaining Proper DWV Pipe Slope

Maintaining correct horizontal pipe slope is critical for consistent waste transport in gravity drainage systems. If a drain pipe lacks adequate pitch, wastewater moves too slowly, allowing heavy suspended solids to settle and build up over time. Conversely, an excessively steep pipe pitch allows liquid waste to flow ahead of solid matter, stranding solids in the pipe interior. Professional installers strictly follow local building codes and verify pipe grade using torpedo levels or laser levels during hanger installation, ensuring water and solids move together smoothly without causing siphoning or structural blockages.
